title: Intrinsic finite-Tor constructibility under quotient extension
statement: For any scheme T, prime ell and r>=m>=1, the actual proScalar quotient extension from the double-lifted coefficient ring at r to that at m preserves IsCtf [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps]. No Noetherianity or prime-invertibility assumption on T is used.

source.place: Intrinsic finite-Tor constructibility under quotient extension; the two-level argument.

proof.text: Convert the ordered homology interval of IsCtf to boundedness. Identify fixed constructible homology with the native fixed-module predicate. The existing comparison criterion produces native constructibleFiniteTor.

Use reductionGood_realization_iff and reductionGood_scalar with the ell^r and ell^m annihilators. The canonical scalarPresentation isomorphism identifies intrinsic scalar extension with the actual fixed proScalar. Transport ReductionGood along it, then apply realization_iff backwards. Convert native bounded constructibility to intrinsic constructibility. Replace unordered endpoint witnesses by min/max to recover the ordered homology and Tor intervals in IsCtf.

theorem quotientIntrinsicCtf
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (r m : ℕ) (_hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmr : m ≤ r)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (K : proCategory (coefficient ell r) T)
    (hK : IsCtf (coefficient ell r) T K) :
    IsCtf (coefficient ell m) T
      ((proScalar (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hmr) T).obj K)
